ai.title: Improve Freebuff session limit messaging
ai.summary: LimitedLandingPanel renders plain-text explanation instead of CTA when quota exhausted. WaitingRoomScreen passes dynamic reset countdown message. Covers CLI components.

eli5.text: When you've hit the free daily session limit, the screen now shows a clear explanation of when your allowance will reset, including a live countdown of the hours remaining, instead of just a generic disabled message. This only affects the free tier of users who've used up their allotted sessions; the screen tells them exactly how many they had and how long until they can start again.

ai.title: Add CURRENTDATE placeholder to agent runtime templates
ai.summary: Moved date formatting from base2.ts to agent-runtime strings.ts via new CURRENT_DATE placeholder. Resolves static date injection in system prompts by enabling runtime substitution. Updated secret-agent-definition.ts and templates/types.ts to register the new placeholder.

eli5.text: The assistant Buffy now shows today's date in a fresh, properly formatted way inside the system prompt that guides its behavior. Previously the date was baked in with a formatting step that lived in the wrong place, which made it static and harder to update. Now date formatting lives in the shared templating system alongside the other dynamic pieces, and the prompt references it as a placeholder that gets filled in at runtime. What you'd notice: if you look at the prompt, it reads 'Current date: <today's date>' and that date will actually match the day you're running it, instead of being a fixed value from when the code was written.

ai.title: Improve CLI binary spawn error diagnostics
ai.summary: Refactored `main()` and `checkForUpdates()` in `cli/release/index.js` and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js` to use a new `spawnInstalledBinary` helper. This replaces bare `spawn` calls with robust error handling that prints detailed system info (platform, node version, binary path/status) on failure. The update includes specific Windows guidance for antivirus blocks and CPU instruction mismatches, plus a `BINARY_MISSING` check that cleans up stale metadata files.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant and it can't start the helper program it needs, you now get a clearer message that tells you your operating system and setup details, and it gives Windows-specific tips if your antivirus or CPU is the likely cause. This affects anyone running the tool from the command line when the downloaded helper binary is missing or won't launch. If you looked, instead of a generic failure you'd see a short report listing your platform, Node version, where the binary is, and guidance on cleaning up stale installation files, so you can tell whether the file is genuinely gone or blocked by something on your machine.
